title: The range of shares that keeps an option

blocks.text: A bus operator is choosing one of several fleet plans, each scored on two measures to maximize: on-time performance points and emissions points. The operator will pick by a weighted sum with a share $`s`$ on the first measure and $`1 - s`$ on the second, but the managers cannot agree on $`s`$. The analyst wants to show, for each plan, the whole range of shares for which it would be chosen, so that the managers only have to agree on which side of a few numbers they stand.

Write `share_range(scores, k)` in `shares.py`. `scores[j]` is plan $`j`$'s pair of points. Return the closed interval `(low, high)` of shares $`s \in [0, 1]`$ at which plan `k`'s weighted score is at least that of every other plan, or `None` if there is no such share.

Write it in notation first: for one rival $`j`$, what inequality in $`s`$ must hold for plan $`k`$ to score at least as much, and when does it bound $`s`$ from below, from above, or not at all? The answer for all rivals together is what is left of $`[0, 1]`$.

from __future__ import annotations


def share_range(scores: list[tuple[float, float]], k: int) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The shares s in [0, 1] at which candidate k is a best choice for s*first + (1-s)*second.

    `scores` holds each candidate's (first, second) value, both to maximize. Returns (low, high),
    the closed interval of shares at which candidate k scores at least as much as every other
    candidate, or None when there is no such share.
    """
    # TODO: compare candidate k with every other candidate.
    return (0.5, 0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(share_range([(0, 10), (6, 8), (10, 0)], 1))

cases.says: a compromise option is best between the two shares at which it breaks even with its rivals
the range never reaches past a share of 0 or 1
an option that some rival always beats has no range at all
an option tied with an identical rival keeps its range

origin.section: The Plan Moves in Jumps as the Weights Change

concepts: each option holds over an interval of shares bounded by break-even values
